rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with the provided 3BB grade and typical expanded blastocyst features, but it adds several image-specific details (exact ICM location, peripheral blebs, polar body remnants, granular blastocoel content) that may not be reliably verifiable from the image alone.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, oocyte yield, BMI, semen parameters, endometrium, prior biochemical pregnancy, and lifestyle factors with embryo quality and prognosis.

The reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with a clear link from morphology and patient factors to prognosis, though some quantitative adjustments are somewhat subjective and not strictly evidence-derived.

Mostly aligned on SET and general embryo assessment, but includes less guideline-supported suggestions such as routine thrombophilia/immunologic-style workup after a single biochemical pregnancy, ERA after limited failure, and broad PGT-A encouragement in a 32-year-old.

Provides clear practical recommendations for transfer, luteal support, monitoring, lifestyle modification, and future-cycle considerations, though some proposed investigations may be more extensive than typically indicated for this history.
